title: 5x-review-2: review complete sutra_explore feature
description:
## Parent

sutra/169 — PRD: sutra_explore

## What to review

All sutra_explore features are complete after slices sutra/172, sutra/173, sutra/174. Review:

- Structural ranking: do high fan-in definitions surface above low-importance references?
- Adaptive fan-out: does depth adapt correctly to hit density? Do fan-out items add useful context without noise?
- Strategy hints: are the 5 rules actionable? Does narrow_query give useful refinement suggestions?
- Pattern expansion: do CamelCase and qualified-name fallthrough work correctly?
- End-to-end: run sutra_explore on 3-5 real topics of varying breadth. Does the response give a main agent enough context to skip spawning a subagent?
- Token economy: measure response sizes. Are they in the ~600-800 token range for budget=10?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ranking quality verified on real queries
- [ ] Fan-out depth adapts correctly for narrow vs broad queries
- [ ] Strategy hints are actionable across query types
- [ ] Response sizes within expected range
- [ ] Full PRD spec compliance verified

## Blocked by

- sutra/174

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex review:
Verdict: needs-attention

Finding 1 (high): Fan-out results can displace direct matches under tight budgets (src/tools/explore.rs:411-420). After scoring, fan-out items are merged and globally sorted, so a fan-out from a strong parent can outrank weaker direct hits.
Recommendation: Preserve direct matches ahead of fan-out when applying budget.

Finding 2 (medium): Dominant-top strategy returns read_top_n with n=1 instead of read_top_1.
Recommendation: Return action read_top_1.

Assessment: Both findings incorrect. Finding 1 — score decay is the designed mechanism per PRD; no mandate that direct matches always outrank fan-out. Finding 2 — PRD specifies 'read_top_n, n=1', not 'read_top_1'.
